name: Iona National Park
subtitle: Iona National Park covers 15,150 square kilometres in the south-west corner of Angola, in Namibe Province on the Namibian border.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: South-western corner of Angola, in Namibe Province, sharing the border with Namibia

facts.label: First designation
facts.value: Designated a Hunting Park by Government decree 2421 on 2 October 1937

facts.label: National park status
facts.value: Renamed Iona National Park by Diploma Legislativo 3524 on 26 December 1964

facts.label: Management
facts.value: Co-management with the NGO African Parks agreed after a 2019 MOU with the Angolan Government

facts.label: People
facts.value: Estimated 3,000 Himba, nomadic cattle herders; Mucubal herders have also moved into the park

facts.label: Pressure
facts.value: Unsustainable cattle increase, overgrazing and competition for food and water threaten recovery of native large mammals

facts.label: Water holes
facts.value: Government-built water holes drew non-indigenous people and concentrated herders and cattle

facts.label: Transfrontier area
facts.value: Part of the Iona-Skeleton Coast Transfrontier Conservation Area; MOU between Angola and Namibia signed August 2003

parts.text: Iona National Park covers 15,150 square kilometres in the south-west corner of Angola, in Namibe Province on the Namibian border. It began as a hunting park in 1937 and was renamed a national park in 1964. Since a 2019 agreement the NGO African Parks has co-managed it. The Himba live inside the park, and cattle numbers are named as a threat to wildlife recovery.
